sources.entry: theme.park - A collection of themes/skins for 50 selfhosted apps! (Source Code) MIT CSS

summary.one_liner: theme.park is a collection of CSS themes and skins for dozens of self-hosted apps, such as Sonarr, Plex, Jellyfin and qBittorrent, installed via a Docker image.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a collection of themes/skins for self-hosted applications. It lists a Docker image as the installation method, plus sections for addons, community themes, and adding your own theme options. The README names a long list of supported apps, including media managers (Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr), media servers (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby), download clients (Deluge, qBittorrent, ruTorrent, Transmission, SABnzbd, NZBGet), and dashboards and tools (Organizr, Portainer, Pi-hole, Uptime Kuma, Gitea, Bitwarden). Several entries are marked as deprecated, including Grafana, Monitorr, Webtools, Logarr, PLPP and The Lounge. Screenshots are linked from the theme banners. The README itself is a short index and gives few details on usage beyond the section headings.
use_cases: customize the look of Sonarr or Radarr
dark theme for Plex or Jellyfin
skin self-hosted dashboards like Portainer or Uptime Kuma
themed Docker deployment of media server UIs
how_to_run: Install the theme.park Docker image (see the Installation section of the README)
Enable the theme for a supported app using its theme option, per the README's app sections
notable: Covers about 50 self-hosted apps in one project
Includes a documented way to add your own theme options
Marks some themes as deprecated, such as Grafana and Monitorr
caveats: Several themes are marked deprecated (Grafana, Monitorr, Webtools, Logarr, PLPP, The Lounge)
The README is a brief index and gives little setup detail in the text provided
keywords: make my media server look nicer
